evidence: Gai. Inst. 3.88: omnis enim obligātiō vel ex contractū nāscitur vel ex dēlictō
terms.comment: The jurists’ word, not in Cicero (Lewis & Short); Traupman uses it of a builder’s contract (cūrābō ut contractus cōnscrībātur, p. 163).

terms.gloss: a written contract to pay, a bond
evidence: Cic. Mur. 35: ex syngraphā agere, to sue on a bond (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The lexicon’s word for a cheque (see cheque).

phrases.latin: omnis enim obligātiō vel ex contractū nāscitur vel ex dēlictō
phrases.english: for every obligation arises either from a contract or from a wrong
I’ll see to it that the contract is drawn up.

sources: Lewis & Short: contractus · Lewis & Short: syngrapha
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 163, 296.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. contract; bond (financial).
Enrico Levi and Arturo Bini, Il latino come lingua viva (1937), p. 18 (contratto).
